content: Landed in Dublin. The air feels different – crisp and damp, not like home at all. Exhausted from the flight but buzzing with a nervous energy. Found my accommodation near UCD, it's basic but it's mine for now. The sheer greenness of everything driving from the airport was striking. Already feeling a bit overwhelmed thinking about the MSc, the people, the unknown. Called Mom and Dad, tried to sound confident but pretty sure they heard the wobble in my voice. Need to unpack and maybe find somewhere to eat that isn't airport food. Tomorrow, UCD orientation. Deep breaths.

Orientation Day 1. Campus is massive, definitely need the map. Attended the welcome talk for international students. So many faces from all over the world. Felt a strange mix of excitement and loneliness. Got my student card (UCard). Went to the bank to try and open an account – need proof of address, which is slightly tricky. The bureaucracy begins! Found a small Indian grocery store nearby, bought some familiar spices. Small comfort.

Met Rohan today at the Computer Science specific orientation. He's from Bangalore, doing the same Negotiated Learning MSc. Instant relief finding someone in the exact same boat. We exchanged numbers and complained about SIM card activation issues. He seems cool, quite knowledgeable already about the modules. We grabbed lunch at the UCD student centre cafe. Overpriced sandwiches, but good conversation.

Finished orientation week. It was a whirlwind. Attended talks on plagiarism, library resources, careers service. Signed up for the UCD Indian Society (IndSoc) and the International Students' Society. Went to a 'speed friending' event – awkward but met a few people, including Kenji from Japan. Trying to remember names is impossible. Feeling slightly more oriented but also aware the real work starts next week.

First day of lectures. Distributed Systems (DS) with Prof. O'Malley is intense from minute one. Concepts like vector clocks flew by. Cloud Computing seems okay, familiar AWS intro. Big Data lecture was interesting, talked about the 3 Vs. ML intro was mostly math refresher - linear algebra hurts. Text Analytics seems practical. Head is spinning trying to process it all. Found the James Joyce library - huge and intimidating.

content: Trying to establish a routine. Wake up, quick breakfast, cycle to UCD (bought a second-hand bike, Dublin drivers are scary!), lectures, library, cycle back, attempt to cook something edible, call home, sleep. Repeat. The DS readings are dense academic papers. Started a study group chat with Rohan. Weather is mostly grey and drizzly. Missing sunshine.

First lab session for Cloud Computing. Setting up an AWS account and spinning up an EC2 instance. Felt good to do something practical. Text Analytics lab involved using NLTK in Python for tokenization. Enjoying the hands-on parts more than the pure theory. Met Aoife in the Text Analytics lab, she's Irish and friendly. Helped her with a Python error.

Went to the IndSoc 'Chai and Chat'. Nice to just relax and speak Hindi/Tamil. Lots of seniors giving advice (mostly warnings) about specific modules and the job market. Feeling a bit more connected to the Indian community here. Still feels weird being a minority though. Cooked rajma chawal tonight, tasted almost like Mom's. Almost.

Distributed Systems assignment 1 released. Consensus algorithms - Paxos and Raft. Looks terrifying. Spent hours reading the Paxos paper, still feels opaque. Rohan and I booked a library study room for the weekend. Need to tackle this together. Feeling the first real wave of academic pressure.

Weekend spent mostly in the library with Rohan. Whiteboard sessions trying to understand Paxos roles (proposers, acceptors, learners). It's slowly making sense, but implementing even a simulation seems hard. Took a break Sunday evening, went for a walk around campus. It's surprisingly peaceful when it's less crowded. Need to manage stress better.

Submitted the DS assignment. Felt like sending a child off to war. Hope it's okay. Immediately started on the Cloud Computing assignment – deploying a simple web app using Elastic Beanstalk. Much more straightforward, thankfully. Attended an International Students' Society event with Kenji. Tried some Irish snacks. Still finding my feet socially.

Feeling the pace pick up. Lectures, labs, readings, assignments... it's relentless. Machine Learning is covering linear regression, cost functions, gradient descent. The math is dense but seeing it implemented in code helps. Started looking into the UCD Careers Network resources. Need to polish my CV soon.

Midterm talk is starting. Need to start revising soon. Big Data concepts (HDFS, MapReduce) are clicking better now. Had a group meeting for the Text Analytics project (sentiment analysis). Group includes Aoife. Seems like a good team. Explored Dublin city centre a bit more over the weekend. Walked down Grafton Street, saw the Molly Malone statue. It's a very walkable city.

Received feedback on DS Assignment 1. Got a B-. Comments highlighted gaps in my understanding of edge cases in Paxos. Slightly disappointed, but it was tough. Need to work harder. Rohan got a B. We discussed the feedback, helps to learn from mistakes. Cloud assignment submitted. Weather is getting noticeably colder. Bought a warmer jacket.

Attended a CV workshop by the Careers Network. Realised how different the expectations are here compared to India. Need quantifiable achievements, STAR method for examples. Started reworking my CV completely. Feels like another assignment. Looked at some job portals (LinkedIn, IrishJobs.ie) – overwhelming number of postings.

Midterm revision in full swing. Focusing on DS and ML. Library is becoming my second home. Rohan and I are quizzing each other. Found a decent coffee place on campus that helps fuel the late nights. Feeling the pressure but trying to stay organised. Cooked a big batch of dal to last a few days – survival mode cooking.

Had the DS midterm. It was tough. Lots of conceptual questions about consistency models and failure detection. Think I managed okay, but hard to say. ML midterm tomorrow. Feeling slightly better prepared for that one, practised implementing algorithms. Need a good night's sleep.

ML midterm done. Covered regression, classification basics (like SVM), gradient descent variants. Felt more manageable than DS. Now just need to get through the Big Data and Text Analytics midterms later this week. Feeling drained. Planned a weekend trip to Howth with Rohan and Kenji as a post-midterm reward.

Finished all midterms! Cloud Computing one was online, quite practical. Text Analytics involved applying techniques like TF-IDF. Brain feels like mush. Looking forward to the Howth trip tomorrow. Need the sea air. Started tentatively applying for a couple of summer internships listed on the career portal. Just testing the waters.

Howth was amazing! The cliff walk offered stunning views of the Irish Sea, even with the wind. Felt refreshing to be out in nature. Had fantastic fish and chips. Good chats with Rohan and Kenji, nice to just hang out without academic pressure. Took lots of photos to send home. Definitely need to explore more of Ireland.

Back to the grind. Second half of the semester feels daunting. Final projects and exams loom large. Started working on the Big Data project – analysing a large dataset using Spark. Need to set up the environment first. Attended a talk by a Google engineer organised by the CS society. Inspiring but also intimidating.

Text Analytics group project is progressing. We're doing sentiment analysis on movie reviews. Aoife is great at structuring the report. I'm focusing on the feature engineering and model training (trying a simple Naive Bayes first). Group work requires coordination, but sharing the load helps. Still sending out internship applications – maybe 2-3 per week.

Received my first rejection email for an internship. Generic, polite. Still stings. Rohan got one too. Misery loves company, I guess. Trying to stay positive. It's a numbers game. Focused on the Cloud Computing project – building a more complex microservice architecture. Learning about Docker containers.

Midterm results are out. DS: C+, ML: B, Cloud: A-, Text Analytics: B+, Big Data: B. Mixed bag. The C+ in DS hurts, need to really buckle down for the final. Happy with the A- in Cloud. Overall passing, which is the main thing, but hoped for better. Need to strategize for finals.

Went for a walk in Phoenix Park with Kenji. Saw the deer up close! It's such a vast green space, easy to forget you're in a city. Good way to de-stress. Talked about career plans. He's interested in game development. Started outlining the final report for the Text Analytics project.

Feeling overwhelmed by the workload again. DS final project involves implementing a distributed key-value store. ML project is about comparing different classification algorithms. Big Data Spark project requires careful optimization. Cloud project needs documentation. And final exams are coming. Need more hours in the day.

content: Attended a workshop on technical interviews. Covered data structures, algorithms, Big O notation. Realised how much I need to practice LeetCode style questions for software engineering roles. Started doing one easy problem a day. It's a different kind of thinking.

Dublin is getting festive, Christmas lights everywhere. It's pretty, but makes me miss Diwali back home intensely. Video called family, they showed me the decorations. Felt a pang of homesickness. Trying to focus on studies. Presented the Text Analytics project with the group – went smoothly.

Received another rejection. And another one. Job hunting is demoralising. Rohan suggested focusing on specific companies and networking on LinkedIn. Sent connection requests to some UCD alumni working at companies I like. Feels awkward but necessary. Spent the weekend working on the DS key-value store implementation. Debugging distributed systems is painful.

Final push before exams. Submitting final projects for Cloud, Big Data, ML. Lots of late nights writing reports and checking code. The relief after each submission is immense. Now, full focus on revising for final exams. Starting with Distributed Systems – my nemesis. Booked flight home for the break! Counting down the days.

Final exam week begins. DS final was as hard as expected. Lots of focus on consistency, replication, failure scenarios. Hoping I scraped a pass. Cloud Computing exam was fair, lots of scenario-based questions about AWS services. Feeling exhausted. Just want this to be over.

ML final done. Covered more advanced topics like ensemble methods and dimensionality reduction. Felt challenging but okay. Big Data exam focused on Spark and Hadoop ecosystem. Text Analytics was application-oriented. That's it! Semester 1 exams are finished! Unbelievable feeling of relief. Going out for a celebratory dinner with Rohan and Aoife tonight.

Packed up, cleaned my room. Said temporary goodbyes. Heading to the airport. Excited to go home, see family, eat mum's food, speak my own language without thinking. Dublin, it's been intense. See you in January.

Home! The warmth, the noise, the smells – it's overwhelming in the best way. Hugged my parents so tight. Jet lag is hitting but don't care. Eating everything in sight. Catching up with cousins and friends. Feels surreal being back after navigating Dublin life.

Relaxing at home. Trying not to think about UCD too much, but also need to choose Semester 2 modules soon. Options include Deep Learning, Generative AI, SQL, Data Science, Speech Processing... all sound interesting but demanding. Leaning towards DL, Gen AI, SQL, Data Science, and Speech. Seems like a heavy load but covers key areas.

Got Semester 1 results online. DS: C (Passed! Relief!), Cloud: A-, ML: B+, Big Data: B, Text Analytics: A-. Overall happy! The A- in Text Analytics was a pleasant surprise. The C in DS was expected but still a huge relief to have passed. Confirmed my Semester 2 module choices. Feeling motivated for the next term.

content: Last few days at home. Saying goodbye is hard. Stocked up on snacks and spices to take back. Feeling apprehensive about going back to the cold and the intensity, but also looking forward to the new modules, especially Gen AI. Promised Mom I'd call more often.

Back in Dublin. The grey skies welcomed me back. Unpacked, tried to make my room feel homely again. It's quiet compared to home. Met up with Rohan for coffee, good to catch up. He's excited about Deep Learning too. Need to get back into the study mindset.

Semester 2 lectures started. Deep Learning (DL) is diving straight into neural networks, activation functions, backpropagation. Professor seems good but expects a lot. Generative AI & Language Models (Gen AI) with Prof. Kavanagh is immediately engaging – talking about the history and potential. SQL is very practical, starting with basic queries. Data Science builds on ML. Speech & Audio Processing is fascinatingly different.

content: Trying to balance the new modules. DL requires strong calculus and linear algebra recall. Gen AI involves reading cutting-edge papers already. SQL labs are fun, getting hands-on with databases. Data Science assignment 1 released – data cleaning focus. Speech processing lab involved plotting waveforms in Python. Busy week.

Got an email invite for a first-round interview! Data Analyst Intern role at a Dublin tech company. Mix of panic and excitement. Scheduled for next week. Need to seriously brush up on SQL, probability, stats, and basic Python coding. Rohan is helping me practice interview questions. He also applied for a few roles.

Weekend spent prepping for the interview and trying to keep up with DL concepts (gradient descent optimization). The interview is tomorrow morning. Feeling nervous. Tried to pick out a smart shirt. It's just a first round, trying not to put too much pressure on myself. Cooked a comforting dal, stress eating slightly.

Had the interview (online). Technical part covered SQL joins, aggregations, a simple Python coding task (string manipulation), and a probability brain teaser. Then behavioural questions ('Why this company?', 'Teamwork example'). Felt I answered okay, maybe stumbled a bit on the probability one. Hard to read the interviewer. Now the waiting game. Back to Gen AI lecture – discussing Word Embeddings (Word2Vec). Fascinating stuff.

Deep Learning assignment 1: Implement a simple neural network from scratch using NumPy to classify MNIST digits. Challenging but rewarding when it starts working. Debugging matrix multiplication dimensions is tricky. Gen AI readings on RNNs and LSTMs for sequence modeling. Complex but powerful. Still waiting to hear back about the interview. Trying not to check emails every 5 minutes.

Rejection email arrived for the Data Analyst role. 'Very competitive... other candidates...' Standard stuff. Still feels rubbish. Talked to Aoife about it, she was encouraging. Need to just keep applying and learning. Focused on the SQL assignment – writing complex queries with subqueries and window functions. It's like solving puzzles.

Data Science assignment submitted (data cleaning and exploration). Started working on the Speech & Audio lab – feature extraction (MFCCs). It's interesting applying signal processing concepts. Sent out another 5-6 internship applications. Tailoring cover letters takes time. Feeling a bit ground down by the cycle.

Got an invite for an online coding assessment! Software Engineer Intern role at a big tech company. Need to practice LeetCode seriously now. Rohan shared his list of common topics (Arrays, Strings, HashMaps, Linked Lists, Trees). Feeling the pressure but also a flicker of hope. Gen AI lecture on Attention mechanism – blew my mind. Starting to see how these models get so powerful.

Weekend spent grinding LeetCode problems. Focused on medium difficulty questions involving arrays and hash maps. It's tough but satisfying when you get the optimal solution. Also trying to keep up with Deep Learning lectures on Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs). Visualising filters and pooling layers is key.

Did the coding assessment. 90 minutes, 2 questions. One was a medium string manipulation problem, felt I solved it well. The other was a harder graph traversal problem, only managed a brute-force solution, couldn't optimize in time. Fingers crossed the first one is enough. Feeling mentally drained. Rewarded myself with pizza.

Started thinking about the Gen AI project. Prof. Kavanagh encourages ambitious ideas. Considering fine-tuning a pre-trained language model like GPT-2 on a specific domain. Maybe UCD course descriptions, or Irish news headlines? Need to research feasibility and datasets. Discussed ideas with Rohan, he's thinking about something with image generation (StyleGAN maybe).

Reading Week next week. Plan is to catch up on DL lectures, do more LeetCode practice, and maybe take one day completely off for a trip. Aoife suggested Glendalough. Need a break from screens. Still no word on the coding assessment result. The uncertainty is gnawing.

Reading week Day 1. Forced myself to revise CNN architectures – LeNet, AlexNet, VGG. It's a lot to remember. Did a couple of LeetCode tree problems. Felt productive but also slightly burnt out already. Need that day trip.

Trip to Glendalough with Aoife and a couple of her friends. Weather was surprisingly decent. The valley, the lakes, the monastic ruins – absolutely beautiful and peaceful. Exactly what I needed. Felt good to just walk, talk, and not think about code or models for a few hours. Took some nice pictures.

Passed the coding assessment! Email arrived this morning. Invited for a technical phone screen next week. Huge relief and excitement. Need to prepare talking through my thought process while coding. Also, bizarrely, got another interview invite today – Cloud Support Engineer Intern. Suddenly things are moving on the job front! Juggling prep for both now, plus regular coursework.

Prepping for the technical screen. Practicing explaining solutions out loud. Focusing on data structures (Trees, Graphs seem common). Also reviewing basic cloud concepts for the other interview. Deep Learning assignment 2 involves implementing a CNN for image classification (CIFAR-10). Using PyTorch this time. Steeper learning curve than NumPy but more powerful.

Had the technical phone screen for the SWE role. Shared coding environment, solved a problem related to finding paths in a matrix (DFS/BFS). Felt I communicated my approach reasonably well. Interviewer seemed engaged. Fingers crossed. Had the Cloud Support interview yesterday – more behavioural and scenario-based ('How would you handle an angry customer?', 'Troubleshoot a connectivity issue'). Felt that one went quite smoothly. More waiting now!

Decided on my Gen AI project: Fine-tuning GPT-2 on UCD module descriptions to generate novel/creative descriptions. Found a dataset on the UCD website that I can scrape and clean. Seems challenging but very relevant to the course. Prof. Kavanagh seemed enthusiastic about the idea during office hours. Started setting up the Python environment (Hugging Face Transformers library).

Got an OFFER! For the Cloud Support Engineer Internship! Received the email this afternoon. Read it three times to be sure. Huge wave of relief washed over me. It's a well-known company, good experience, and it means I have *something* secured for the summer. Called parents, they were relieved too. Celebrated with Rohan and Aoife at the campus bar. A weight has definitely lifted.

Still waiting to hear back from the SWE final round invite after the phone screen. The Cloud offer makes the wait less agonizing, but the SWE role is still the one I'd prefer. Trying to focus on the Deep Learning CNN assignment, getting decent accuracy on CIFAR-10 now after tweaking hyperparameters. It's satisfying when the loss goes down.

Email arrived! Made it to the final round for the Software Engineer Intern role! It's a virtual 'on-site' loop – multiple interviews back-to-back covering coding, system design, and behavioural aspects. Scheduled in two weeks. Okay, deep breaths. This is the big one. Need to seriously prepare system design concepts now. How to scale websites? Database choices? Caching strategies? Feels like a huge step up.

Weekend spent cramming System Design. Watched YouTube videos, read articles ('Grokking the System Design Interview' seems popular). It's fascinating but also vast. Trying to understand trade-offs. Also started working on the Gen AI project – data scraping and cleaning is tedious but crucial. Got a decent dataset of module descriptions now.

Data Science group project presentation today. We analyzed flight delay data and built a classification model. Went well, the team worked effectively together. Aoife did a great job presenting our findings. Feeling more comfortable with the end-to-end data science workflow now (cleaning, EDA, modeling, evaluation). SQL practical exam next week. Need to be quick with queries.

SQL practical exam done. Had to write several complex queries against a sample database within a time limit. Felt confident about most of them. Final round SWE interviews tomorrow. Feeling incredibly nervous. Did some mock interviews with Rohan. Trying to stay calm and just do my best.

Interview day. Four back-to-back virtual interviews. 2x Coding, 1x System Design, 1x Behavioural (with hiring manager). Coding rounds were medium/hard LeetCode style, felt okay on one, struggled slightly on the other but talked through my approach. System design was designing a basic URL shortener – discussed APIs, database schema, hashing, caching. Behavioural was standard. Brain completely fried afterwards. Exhausted. They said expect to hear back in a week or so.

content: Trying to distract myself while waiting for the SWE interview result. Deep dive into the Gen AI project. Set up the fine-tuning script using Hugging Face trainer. Started a small run on a subset of the data using UCD's computing resources (thankfully available!). Seeing the model generate slightly more coherent text is thrilling. Debugging CUDA errors is not.

Got the call. GOT THE OFFER! Software Engineer Intern! I actually yelled out loud when the recruiter told me. Unbelievable. It's my top choice company here in Dublin. The role sounds perfect. Called Mom and Dad immediately, they were overjoyed. Huge relief and happiness. Accepted the offer formally via email. Now need to politely withdraw from the Cloud Support role.

Officially accepted the SWE offer and withdrew from the other one. Felt a bit bad, but it was the right move. Celebrated properly with Rohan, Aoife, Kenji (who is preparing to leave soon) – went out for dinner. Feels amazing to have the job search over and to have landed a role I'm genuinely excited about. Now, can focus 100% on smashing the final exams and projects, especially making the Gen AI one really good.

Final project work intensifying. Deep Learning project is implementing an image captioning model (CNN encoder, RNN decoder). Complex architecture, lots of moving parts in PyTorch. Speech & Audio project is building a basic speaker identification system using GMMs on MFCC features. Gen AI fine-tuning is running on the full dataset now, results look promising, generating quite creative (and sometimes funny) module descriptions. Need to start writing the reports soon.

content: Starting final exam revision. Semester 2 feels even more packed than Sem 1. Revising Deep Learning architectures (RNNs, LSTMs, Transformers, CNNs), Data Science concepts (evaluation metrics, feature selection), SQL advanced topics, Speech processing fundamentals. The Gen AI exam will likely be more conceptual/ethical, need to review lecture notes and key papers (like 'Attention is All You Need').

Exam week begins. Data Science exam was theory-heavy but fair. SQL exam was similar to the practical but maybe slightly easier. Speech & Audio exam involved signal processing maths and understanding feature extraction pipelines. Juggling revision with final tweaks to projects.

Deep Learning exam today. Very challenging. Focused heavily on understanding architectures, backpropagation through time, attention mechanisms. Think I did enough to pass, hopefully better. Gen AI exam tomorrow – last one! Feeling tired but motivated to finish strong. Spent the evening writing the conclusion for the Gen AI project report.

Gen AI exam done! It was essay-based, covering topics like evaluating generative models, ethical implications, limitations of current LLMs, and future directions. Felt I could draw heavily on my project experience and the papers we discussed. That's it! All exams finished! The relief is immense. Just need to submit the final projects now.

Final project submission day. Submitted DL (Image Captioning), Speech (Speaker ID), and Gen AI (GPT-2 fine-tuning). Put a lot of effort into the Gen AI report, detailing the process, results, generated examples, and limitations. Feels good to have it all handed in. The culmination of the semester's work. Feeling proud, especially of the Gen AI project. Completely exhausted now. Time for a break.

Catching up on sleep! Started cleaning my room properly, feels like emerging from a bunker. Met Rohan for lunch, we just chatted about non-academic stuff for hours. Felt normal again. Waiting for results is always nerve-wracking, but less so now with the job secured. Planning some trips around Ireland for the summer.

Results are out! Logged in with trembling hands. Passed everything! DL: B+, SQL: A, Data Science: A-, Speech: B+. And then... Generative AI & Language Models: A+ !! Stared at the screen for a minute. An A+! Absolutely ecstatic. The hard work on that project really paid off. Prof. Kavanagh's comment was lovely too. Called family immediately, they were so proud. Easily the academic highlight of the year. HUGE confidence boost.

Still buzzing from the A+ result. Shared the news with Aoife and Kenji too. Kenji is leaving next week, planning a farewell get-together. Started looking into the Graduate Scheme visa process – need the official MSc completion letter first, but gathering documents. Also started tentatively looking for shared apartments/houses for when I start the job in September. Dublin rental market looks scary.

Farewell drinks for Kenji. Sad to see him go, but happy for his next steps back in Japan. Exchanged contact details, promised to stay in touch. It's strange how quickly you form bonds in this intense international student environment. Reflecting on the friendships made here. Went to the National Museum of Ireland - Archaeology. The bog bodies and Celtic gold were incredible.

Received the official 'Confirmation of Award' letter from UCD. Needed this for the visa application. Started filling out the online forms for the Third Level Graduate Programme (Stamp 1G). Bureaucracy is never fun, but necessary. Also ramped up the apartment hunting on Daft.ie. Viewings are chaotic, places go so fast.

Weekend trip to Galway with Rohan and Aoife. Rented a car, drove across the country. Explored the city centre, listened to trad music in a pub. Drove out to the Cliffs of Moher the next day – absolutely spectacular, terrifyingly high! Also saw the strange landscape of the Burren. Great craic with them. Going to miss Aoife when she goes travelling.

Submitted the Graduate Scheme visa application online. Now need to book an appointment to register with Garda National Immigration Bureau (GNIB). Appointments seem hard to get. More waiting. Went to a viewing for a room in Rathmines, seemed decent, shared with two young professionals. Fingers crossed.

Got offered the room in Rathmines! Accepted immediately. Signed the lease electronically and paid the deposit. Huge relief to have accommodation sorted for starting work. It's more expensive than student accom, but looks like a nice area. Celebrated with takeaway curry. One major stress factor removed.

Aoife left for her summer travels through Southeast Asia. Said goodbye, promised postcards. Rohan started his internship, seems to be settling in well. Feels like the student chapter is truly closing. Spent the day reading in St Stephen's Green, enjoying the rare Dublin sunshine.

Received my contract and onboarding documents from the company. Start date confirmed for early September. Reading through everything, feels real now! Need to sort out bank details, PPS number etc. Booked my GNIB appointment – earliest was late July, cutting it a bit fine but should be okay.

Trying to keep my technical skills sharp before starting work. Doing some online courses on technologies the company uses (mentioned React in the job description). Also revisiting some concepts from the MSc – maybe try a small personal project using Generative AI? The A+ still feels good. Visited Trinity College and saw the Book of Kells. Touristy but impressive.

content: Went for a hike in the Dublin Mountains (Ticknock). Great views over the city and bay. Felt good to get some exercise. Starting to feel less like a tourist and more like someone who lives here. Had a video call with family, updated them on the job, visa, apartment. They're happy and proud.

Met up with Rohan. He's enjoying his internship work but finding the 9-to-5 routine an adjustment after student life. We grabbed pints near Grand Canal Dock, where many tech companies are. Talked about future plans, career paths. Feels good to have someone who understands the journey.

Visited the Guinness Storehouse. Very commercial but well done. The Gravity Bar view at the end with the complimentary pint is definitely worth it. Felt like ticking off a Dublin bucket list item. Starting to pack up my student room, preparing for the move to Rathmines next week.

GNIB appointment day. Went to the office, submitted documents, fingerprints, photo taken. All went smoothly. Should receive the Irish Residence Permit (IRP) card by post in a couple of weeks. Massive bureaucratic hurdle cleared! Felt like a proper 'adulting' achievement. Celebrated with fancy coffee.

Moving day! Packed my life into a couple of suitcases and bags. Took a taxi to the new house in Rathmines. Met my new housemates properly – seem like nice, normal people. Unpacked in my new room. Feels much more permanent than the student digs. Explored the Rathmines area a bit – lots of shops, cafes, pubs. Feels like a good neighbourhood.

Received my IRP card in the post! Valid for one year. Feels official. Settling into the new house. Arranged Wi-Fi payment with housemates, figuring out bin schedules. The mundane parts of life. Had a video call with Kenji, showed him my new room. He's enjoying being back in Japan.

Received the official MSc degree parchment by post from UCD. Framed it? Maybe later. It’s a tangible reminder of the hard work, the stress, the learning, the A+! Looking forward to the graduation ceremony later in the year. Started doing some pre-reading for my job, familiarizing myself with the team's project area based on the onboarding info.

Took a solo day trip to Bray and walked the cliff path to Greystones. Beautiful coastal walk, less crowded than Howth. Felt reflective, thinking about the whole year – the initial struggles, the friendships formed, the academic challenges overcome, the job success. It's been transformative. Feeling grateful for the experience and excited for what comes next.

Getting ready for the job start. Bought some 'smart casual' clothes (what does that even mean?). Set up my desk area in my room. Feeling a mix of excitement and nerves. It's a new chapter. Met Rohan for a final 'student life' coffee before we both become proper working professionals.

Just over a week until I start the new job. Enjoying the last bit of freedom. Explored the Iveagh Gardens, a hidden gem in the city centre. Reading a novel, not a research paper! Cooked a proper meal in the new kitchen. Dublin feels like home now, a different kind of home. Ready for the next adventure.

First full week of lectures done. Distributed Systems is theoretical hell, Cloud Computing practicals look manageable, Big Data concepts are clicking slowly, Machine Learning math is intense, Text Analytics feels refreshingly applied. Jet lag still messing with sleep. Trying to make sense of the UCD online portal (Brightspace) - so many modules, so many links. Cooked instant noodles again, need to learn actual cooking.

content: Joined a study group for Distributed Systems with Rohan and two others. Trying to decode lecture notes together. It helps, but the pace is relentless. Attended a 'Know Your Rights' workshop for international students. Useful info on visas, accommodation contracts etc. Feeling slightly more empowered but also aware of potential pitfalls. Dublin is expensive! Trying to budget carefully.

Tried exploring beyond the immediate UCD area. Took a bus into the city centre just to wander. Walked along the River Liffey, saw the Ha'penny Bridge. It's a city with character. Felt anonymous but in a good way. Still haven't quite figured out the bus system routes fully. Small steps.

Big Data lab: Setting up a pseudo-distributed Hadoop environment on a VM. Lots of configuration files to edit. Frustrating when it doesn't work, satisfying when it does. Realising how much practical setup is involved before you even get to the algorithms. Talked to Aoife after Text Analytics lecture, she recommended a good place for cheap eats near campus. Need those tips!

Feeling the first wave of homesickness properly hit. It was Dad's birthday yesterday, video call felt inadequate. Seeing everyone celebrating together made me miss home acutely. Poured myself into studying for the DS assignment to distract myself. Listened to some old favourite Hindi songs. It's tough sometimes.

End of September already! The month flew by in a blur of lectures, labs, and trying to settle in. Submitted the DS assignment, hoping for the best. Started looking at the Machine Learning assignment - implementing linear regression and evaluating it. Need to brush up on NumPy and Matplotlib. Feeling slightly more organised than week 1, but the mountain of work ahead is still huge.

Cloud Computing assignment 2: Using more AWS services - S3 for storage, maybe Lambda for serverless functions. The AWS console has so many options! It's easy to get lost. Attended a 'Careers in Tech' panel discussion. Speakers from various companies (startups, multinationals). Interesting perspectives, but also highlighted the competitiveness of the job market. Feeling the pressure to start thinking about internships already.

Weekend exploring. Went to the National Gallery of Ireland. Free entry! Spent a couple of hours looking at art, felt cultured. Met up with Kenji afterwards, wandered through Merrion Square, saw the Oscar Wilde statue. Nice to have casual conversations, comparing notes on Dublin life and studies. He finds Irish slang amusing.

Machine Learning assignment is tricky. Implementing gradient descent requires careful handling of learning rates and feature scaling. Spent ages debugging. Finally got it converging. The practical application makes the theory stick better. Rohan is working on the same assignment, we compared results. Helps to have a sanity check.

Received rejection from one of the first internships I applied to. Didn't even get an interview. Ah well. Back to the CV - trying to rephrase project descriptions using the STAR method as suggested in the workshop. It's hard to quantify academic project achievements sometimes. Booked a library study room for serious midterm revision.

Deep into midterm revision. Flashcards for Distributed Systems concepts. Reworking ML tutorial problems. Reviewing Big Data architectures. It's information overload. Took a short break to walk around the lake on campus. The swans are aggressive! Need to balance intense study with breaks to avoid burnout.

Text Analytics midterm felt okay. Focused on concepts like TF-IDF, vector space models, evaluation metrics (precision, recall). Cloud Computing online midterm also seemed reasonable, testing knowledge of core AWS services. Two down, two (the harder ones - DS, ML) to go. The finish line for midterms is in sight.

Post-midterm relief. Went to a pub recommended by Aoife with her and Rohan. Tried Guinness properly for the first time (mixed feelings!). Good atmosphere, lots of chatter. Nice to socialize and not talk about lectures for a change. Feeling more integrated into the small group of friends.

Started the final project for Cloud Computing - designing and implementing a scalable, fault-tolerant web service. Thinking of using microservices architecture, maybe with Docker Swarm or Kubernetes (if I'm feeling brave). Feels like a good practical challenge. Need to research best practices.

Working on the Big Data Spark project. Processing a large dataset (few GBs) locally is slow. Learning Spark RDDs and DataFrames API. The functional programming style takes some getting used to. Debugging Spark jobs feels like black magic sometimes. Stack Overflow is my best friend.

Attended an IndSoc Diwali event on campus. Lighting lamps, sharing sweets, music. Felt a bit like home for a couple of hours. Good to see so many familiar faces from the Indian community. Talked to some seniors about their job search experiences last year – helpful insights, mostly reinforcing that it's tough but possible.

Machine Learning final project: Comparing performance of different classifiers (e.g., SVM, Random Forest, Logistic Regression) on a chosen dataset. Need to do proper cross-validation and hyperparameter tuning. Applying the concepts learned throughout the semester. Decided to use a dataset from Kaggle.

Received another internship rejection. This one was after an initial automated screening. The process feels impersonal and random sometimes. Trying not to take it personally. Focused on refining my LinkedIn profile, adding project details. Sent a connection request to a recruiter who posted a relevant role. Small actions.

Distributed Systems final project: Implementing a simplified version of a distributed hash table (DHT) like Chord or Kademlia. Deeply theoretical but forces you to understand the protocols inside out. Pair-programming with Rohan on this one, helps to bounce ideas and debug together. Long hours in the CS lab.

Feeling the end-of-semester crunch. Multiple project deadlines approaching, plus final exams looming. Stress levels are high across the board. Trying to maintain a semblance of healthy habits - eating properly, getting *some* sleep. Went for a run around campus just to clear my head. It helped a bit.

Submitted the Cloud Computing final project report and code. One down! Documenting the architecture took almost as long as building it. Started serious revision for the DS final exam. This one scares me the most. Going through lecture notes, past papers (if available), trying to solidify understanding of consensus, replication, consistency models.

Submitted Big Data (Spark) and ML (Classification Comparison) projects. Huge relief. Feels like crossing milestones. Library is packed 24/7 now. The collective stress is palpable. Keeping fueled with coffee and determination. Flight home is booked for the 19th, the light at the end of the tunnel.

Final exam revision mode. Focused entirely on DS and ML for now. Whiteboarding concepts with Rohan. Flashcards deployed. Trying to anticipate question types. It feels like preparing for battle. Limited social life, just study, eat, sleep (maybe).

Text Analytics final exam today. Felt manageable, similar style to midterm but covering more topics (like topic modeling, information extraction). Big Data exam tomorrow. One more after that (ML), then DS. Almost there. Feeling the fatigue but pushing through.

Survived the DS final. It was as challenging as anticipated. Left the exam hall feeling unsure but glad it's over. That marks the end of Semester 1 academic work! The sense of accomplishment is huge, regardless of results. Time to pack and mentally prepare for going home.

Landed back in India. The familiar heat and chaos embraced me. Mom's cooking tastes like heaven. So good to be fussed over by family. Catching up with everyone, sharing stories about Dublin (the edited version!). Jet lag is real but being home overrides it.

Christmas Day. Not a big festival for my family, but enjoyed the quiet day at home. Watched movies, ate well. Reflected on the past few months in Dublin – the challenges, the learning, the new environment. It's been a massive adjustment but feels like I'm growing. Checked UCD emails – finalized Semester 2 modules: DL, Gen AI, SQL, Data Sci, Speech/Audio. Looks excitingly tough.

Meeting up with old friends from undergrad. Feels good to reconnect. Trying to explain the MSc and life abroad. Some are working, some studying further in India. Interesting hearing their perspectives. Makes me appreciate the opportunity I have but also miss the familiarity of home.

Semester 1 results released online. Logged in nervously. Overall B+ average! Passed DS with a C, huge relief. Got an A- in Cloud and Text Analytics! Really happy with that. Boosts my confidence for Semester 2. Shared the news with family, they are proud. Feeling ready to go back and tackle the next set of challenges.

Packing bags again, feels too soon. Said emotional goodbyes to family. Stocked up on homemade snacks. Flying back to Dublin tomorrow. Mixed feelings – sadness leaving home, but also anticipation for the new semester and seeing Dublin friends again.

Back in Dublin. The cold hit me immediately. Unpacked, grocery shopping, tried to get back into the timezone. Flat feels quiet. Met Rohan for coffee, exchanged stories about the break and results. Ready to dive into Semester 2 tomorrow. Let's do this.

First lectures for new modules. Deep Learning is math-heavy but fascinating. Gen AI with Prof Kavanagh is already inspiring, discussing ethics early on. SQL is refreshingly practical. Data Science seems like a good consolidation of ML concepts. Speech/Audio Processing is totally new, involves signals and phonetics. Brain is full.

Getting into the rhythm of Semester 2. DL assignment 1 (NN from scratch) looks intense. Gen AI requires keeping up with recent papers. SQL labs are good practice. Started Data Science assignment 1 (data cleaning with Pandas). Speech labs involve using Praat software. Juggling five modules is tough. Applied for a Data Analyst internship that looked interesting.

content: Republic Day back home. Felt a bit nostalgic. Saw IndSoc posts about celebrations. Couldn't attend as had evening lab. Received email invite for first round interview for the Data Analyst role! Panic/excitement! Need to prep SQL, Python, Stats. Scheduled for Jan 30th.

Interview done yesterday. Waiting game now. Trying to focus on studies. Gen AI lecture on Transformers - complex but crucial architecture. Deep Learning assignment debugging is painful, NumPy array shapes are the bane of my existence right now. Feeling tired but pushing through.

Rejection for the Data Analyst role. Sigh. It's disheartening but expected, I guess. Need to keep applying. Talked to Careers service about interview feedback, they gave some generic tips. Back to LeetCode practice for future SWE roles. Focused on SQL assignment - complex joins and subqueries.

Submitted SQL assignment. Started working on the Data Science project with Aoife and others – predictive modeling task. Speech processing assignment involves implementing MFCC calculation. Interesting but math-heavy. Feeling the workload pile up. Need to stay organised.

Received invite for a coding assessment (SWE Intern). Okay, this is more aligned with my goals. Need to step up LeetCode prep. Focused on Arrays, Strings, Hashmaps as Rohan suggested. Feeling hopeful but also nervous about the timed test format.

Spent Saturday doing LeetCode mediums. It's challenging but also kind of addictive when you solve one. Reviewed common data structures and their time/space complexities. Deep Learning lecture covered CNNs, which seem crucial for image tasks. Trying to balance job prep with understanding complex module content.

Took the coding assessment today. 90 mins, 2 questions. Felt okay about the first (array manipulation), struggled to find the optimal solution for the second (graph problem). Submitted what I had. Hope it's enough. Feeling drained. Ordered takeaway to celebrate surviving it.

Brainstorming Gen AI project ideas more seriously. Fine-tuning GPT-2 seems feasible and interesting. Potential datasets: UCD modules, Irish folklore, news headlines. Need to check data availability and compute resources required. Discussed with Prof. Kavanagh, got positive feedback on the module description idea.

Reading week next week. Plan: 1. Catch up on DL/Gen AI lectures. 2. LeetCode practice. 3. Start Gen AI project setup. 4. Day trip! Aoife suggested Glendalough. Sounds perfect. Still waiting for coding assessment results. The limbo is frustrating.

Reading week. Revised CNNs and started reading about RNNs for Deep Learning. Did some LeetCode linked list and tree problems. Started scraping UCD module descriptions for the Gen AI project. Data cleaning looks like it will be tedious.

content: Glendalough trip today with Aoife's group. Stunningly beautiful, even with the moody Irish weather. The walk around the lakes was refreshing. Good company, good conversations. A much-needed mental reset before the second half of the semester. Ireland's landscape is quite something.

Passed the coding assessment! Got the email yesterday. Invited for a technical phone screen (SWE Intern). Thrilled! Also received an interview invite for a Cloud Support Engineer Intern role at another company. Suddenly have two active processes! Need to prep for both interview styles - technical coding vs. cloud concepts/behavioural. Busy times ahead.

Prepping for interviews. Practicing coding problems on a shared editor simulator. Reviewing AWS fundamentals for the cloud role. Also working on the DL assignment 2 (CNN implementation with PyTorch). PyTorch feels more intuitive than TensorFlow for me so far.

St. Patrick's Day! Dublin is buzzing. Went to see the parade with Rohan and some others. Very green, very loud, lots of people. Interesting cultural experience. Had the Cloud Support interview yesterday - felt conversational, focused on troubleshooting scenarios. Technical screen for SWE role tomorrow. Nervous!

Technical screen done (SWE Intern). Solved a problem involving heaps/priority queues, talked through complexity. Felt I explained my thinking clearly. Fingers crossed. Now need to focus back on UCD work. Gen AI project: started cleaning the scraped module data using Python scripts. Lots of inconsistencies to handle.

content: Received the offer for the Cloud Support Engineer internship! Accepted it as a safety net. HUGE relief knowing I have something secured for summer. Celebrated quietly, still hoping for the SWE role but the pressure is off significantly. Shared the good news with family.

Got the invite for the final round (virtual on-site) for the SWE Intern role! Amazing news! Need to prep system design now. This is the one I really want. Juggling this prep with DL assignment, Gen AI project setup (installing Hugging Face, PyTorch), and Data Science project work. Sleep is becoming a luxury.

content: Deep dive into System Design prep. Concepts like Load Balancing, Database Sharding, Caching, CAP Theorem. It's fascinating but complex. Watching mock interviews online. Trying to structure answers. Also working on the Gen AI project - got the Hugging Face pipeline running for basic text generation with GPT-2. Now to figure out the fine-tuning part.

content: Presented Data Science group project findings. Our model predicting customer churn performed reasonably well. Good teamwork experience with Aoife and the others. Feeling more confident in applying the ML pipeline. SQL practical exam is looming. Need to practice writing queries under time pressure.

Final round SWE interviews tomorrow. Reviewed notes on common coding problems, system design patterns, and prepared STAR examples for behavioural questions. Feeling as ready as I can be, but nerves are definitely high. Did a final mock system design session with Rohan.

content: Survived the final round interviews. Mentally exhausted. System Design was challenging (design a Twitter feed). Coding rounds were okay. Behavioural felt standard. Now the wait begins again. Trying to shift focus back to UCD - specifically the Gen AI fine-tuning experiment. Need to set up the training loop properly.

content: Got the call. GOT THE SWE INTERN OFFER! YES! Absolutely thrilled! Accepted immediately. This is the one! Called family, celebrated with friends. All the LeetCode grinding and stress feels worth it. Politely withdrew from the Cloud Support offer. Feeling on top of the world. Now, finish the MSc strong!

With the job secured, feeling motivated to really ace the final projects. Deep Learning image captioning project is complex but interesting (CNN+LSTM). Speech ID project using GMMs is progressing. The Gen AI fine-tuning is running on the UCD cluster, results are starting to look really good – generating plausible, sometimes creative, module descriptions. Very exciting!

Exam revision starting. Need to cover DL, Gen AI concepts, Data Science theory, SQL, Speech Processing. Busy period ahead but feeling less stressed overall now the job hunt is over. Can focus purely on academics. Writing the report for the Gen AI project, trying to capture the methodology and results clearly.

SQL Exam and Data Science exam done this week. Felt prepared. The practical SQL skills feel very valuable. Data Science theory was broad but manageable. Focused revision now on DL and Gen AI. The Gen AI project report is taking shape, really enjoying analysing the generated text.

Deep Learning exam today. Challenging, covered a lot of architectures and concepts. Hope I did okay. Gen AI exam tomorrow - last one! Reviewing ethical considerations, evaluation metrics for generative models, key papers. Feeling good about this subject thanks to the project.

All exams finished! Final projects submitted yesterday - DL, Speech, and the Gen AI one I'm quite proud of. Huge sense of relief and accomplishment. Semester 2 was intense but incredibly rewarding, especially Gen AI. Time to relax and wait for results.

Catching up on sleep and life admin. Started looking into the visa process for the graduate scheme (Stamp 1G). Need the final transcript/letter from UCD first. Explored the Dublin Flea Market over the weekend, interesting finds. Nice to have free time again.

Results day! Logged on nervously... Passed all! And... A+ in Generative AI and Language Models! Absolutely stunned and overjoyed! All that work on the fine-tuning project paid off beyond expectations. Professor Kavanagh's comment was incredibly encouraging. Best academic result ever. Called family, they were ecstatic. What a high note to end the MSc on!

Still buzzing about the A+. Received the official confirmation of award eligibility from UCD. Started the Graduate Scheme visa application process online. Also started the dreaded Dublin apartment hunt on Daft.ie. Looks like a nightmare. Need to find a place before the job starts in Sept.

Farewell gathering for Kenji. Sad to see him leave Dublin. Exchanged contacts, promised to visit Japan someday (and vice versa). Reflecting on the international friendships formed here. Started attending apartment viewings – crowded, competitive, expensive. This is going to be tough.

Weekend trip to Galway booked with Rohan and Aoife as a final adventure before life changes (Aoife travelling, Rohan and I starting work/internships). Looking forward to seeing the West Coast. Submitted the visa application online, now waiting for appointment availability. Apartment hunt continues to be demoralising.

Galway trip was fantastic! Cliffs of Moher were breathtaking. Driving through the Burren was surreal. Galway city has a great vibe. Perfect escape and bonding time with Rohan and Aoife. Back in Dublin, secured a GNIB appointment for late July. Cutting it fine for the visa, but should be okay. Found a potential room share in Rathmines, viewing tomorrow.

Got the room in Rathmines! Signed the lease, paid deposit. Huge relief! Accommodation sorted. Now I can relax a bit more about the logistics. Celebrated by cooking a big meal. Rathmines seems like a nice area, well-connected.

Said goodbye to Aoife as she heads off travelling. Going to miss her! Rohan started his internship, sounds busy but interesting. Feels like the end of the UCD chapter. Started sorting through notes, deciding what to keep. Received job contract, reviewing and signing.

Keeping busy to avoid post-MSc slump. Working through some online tutorials related to the tech stack at my new job (React, Node.js). Visited Kilmainham Gaol - fascinating and sobering piece of Irish history. Reading for pleasure again!

GNIB appointment went smoothly. Submitted biometrics, photo taken. Should get the IRP card in 2-3 weeks. Another major hurdle cleared. Feeling more secure about the post-study work process. Went for a walk along Dun Laoghaire pier. Lovely coastal town feel.

Packing up student accommodation. Lots of memories in this small room. Exciting to be moving to a new place. Coordinated moving logistics for next week. Had a final UCD campus walk with Rohan, reminiscing about the past year.

Moved into the Rathmines house! Met housemates, seem friendly. Unpacked, starting to make the room my own. Feels good to have a proper base. Explored the local shops. Ordered pizza for the first night dinner. A new chapter begins.

Received IRP card! Stamp 1G secured. Officially allowed to work. Huge relief. Also received the MSc degree parchment from UCD. Feels very official. Thinking about framing it. Started setting up utilities/bills in the new house share. Adulting continues.

Enjoying exploring Rathmines and nearby areas like Ranelagh. Lots of nice cafes and restaurants. Trying to establish a new routine before work starts. Doing some light coding practice, reviewing fundamentals. Less pressure now, more curiosity-driven learning.

Had a call with my future manager. Discussed onboarding plan, team projects. Sounds like interesting work, using modern technologies. Feeling excited and slightly intimidated. Asked about pre-reading materials they could share.

Took a weekend trip to Belfast, Northern Ireland. Visited the Titanic Museum, saw the Peace Walls. Very different history and atmosphere compared to Dublin. Interesting to see another part of the island. Train journey was scenic.

Received some onboarding documents and links to internal tech talks from my manager. Spending some time going through them. Also enjoying the last few weeks of complete freedom. Reading, exploring parks (Iveagh Gardens, Herbert Park), trying new recipes.

Met Rohan for drinks. He finishes his internship soon too. We talked about starting our full-time roles, future plans, maybe finding our own place eventually instead of house shares. Good to have someone on the same wavelength.

Feeling reflective as the MSc year truly ends and the work chapter begins. Landed here almost exactly a year ago, nervous and overwhelmed. Now, have a Master's degree with a highlight A+, a great job starting soon, good friends, explored a new country, found a place to live. Huge personal and professional growth. Grateful for the entire UCD experience, challenges and all.

Bought some work clothes. Preparing mentally for the 9-to-5 (or likely more) routine. Setting up my workspace at home for potential hybrid work days. Less than two weeks to go! Excitement is building.

Final weekend of freedom. Went for a long walk on Dollymount Strand. Trying to soak up the last bits of unstructured time. Feeling ready and eager to start the job, apply everything I've learned, and continue learning. Dublin feels like home now. The next adventure starts Monday.

Distributed Systems concepts like vector clocks and logical time are still confusing. Spent extra time in the library trying to grasp them. Attended an optional tutorial session which helped clarify things a bit. Realizing this module requires consistent effort, can't just cram it.

Got feedback on the ML assignment (linear regression). Did well, B+. Comments suggested exploring regularization techniques, which we haven't covered in detail yet but good to know for future. Small wins like this help maintain motivation amidst the overall stress.

Feeling the pressure of the upcoming DS final exam. It covers the entire semester's worth of challenging concepts. Formed a small, intense study group with Rohan and two others just for this module. We're planning marathon revision sessions over the next few days.

Spent Sunday prepping for the Data Analyst interview. Practiced SQL queries on HackerRank, reviewed probability rules, and rehearsed answers to common behavioural questions using the STAR method. Feels like preparing for an exam, but with higher stakes potentially.

Speech & Audio processing lab on Phonetics and Praat software. Analysing recordings of vowels, looking at formants. It's fascinating how speech sounds can be broken down and visualized. Completely different from other CS modules. Offers a nice change of pace mentally.

Reading papers for Generative AI - specifically looking at the original GAN paper. The adversarial training concept is ingenious but notoriously tricky to get stable. Trying to understand the math behind the loss functions. Feels like research work more than undergrad learning.

Working on the Deep Learning CNN assignment (CIFAR-10 classification). Experimenting with different architectures (adding more conv layers, dropout, batch norm). Seeing the accuracy improve with each tweak is satisfying. PyTorch is growing on me.

System design prep continues. Trying to understand trade-offs between different database types (SQL vs NoSQL), consistency models (strong vs eventual), and when to use message queues or caching. It's less about 'right' answers and more about justifying choices.

Withdrew from the Cloud Support offer politely, thanking them for their time. Felt slightly awkward but necessary. Received the official written offer letter for the SWE role. Reading the details (salary, benefits, start date) makes it feel very real. Excitement levels are high!

Submitted the Deep Learning final project (Image Captioning). The model generates some reasonable captions, but also some nonsensical ones. Training convergence was tricky. Writing the report involved explaining the CNN-RNN architecture and the challenges faced. Glad it's done.

Final project submitted: Speech ID system. Used MFCCs and GMMs. Accuracy was okay for a small set of speakers. Learned a lot about audio feature extraction and basic pattern recognition techniques for speech. Another module completed.

Went to Howth again, this time solo. Needed some quiet reflection time after the intensity of exams and results. Walked the cliffs, watched the sea. Felt a sense of peace and accomplishment. Thinking about how much has changed in less than a year.

Apartment hunting is proving very difficult. High demand, high rents. Attended several viewings, often with 20+ other people. Feeling discouraged. Need to find something before September. Exploring different neighbourhoods - Ranelagh, Portobello, Rathmines seem popular but pricey.

Said goodbye to Aoife before her travels. Exchanged gifts. Will miss our chats and her local insights. Friendships formed during intense experiences like this MSc feel strong. Hope we stay in touch across the distance.

Received the IRP card (visa) in the mail! Such a relief to have the physical card and know the Stamp 1G is fully processed. One less thing to worry about before starting work. Updated my LinkedIn profile to 'MSc Computer Science Graduate'. Feels good.

Reading some documentation provided by my future manager about the team's codebase and current projects. Trying to get a head start, even if it's just understanding the terminology and architecture diagrams. Feeling proactive but also trying to enjoy the remaining downtime.

One year anniversary of arriving in Dublin. Incredible how fast time has flown and how much has happened. From feeling lost and overwhelmed to having completed the MSc, secured a great job, built friendships, and found a place to live. Immense gratitude for the journey. Ready for the next chapter.

Trying to navigate UCD's VLE (Brightspace). Each module has its own section, lecture notes, assignments, forums. It's a lot to keep track of. Set up calendar reminders for deadlines. Found the student gym - looks good, might join to de-stress.

First Distributed Systems assignment submitted. Felt like climbing a mountain. Celebrated with Rohan by getting pizza. Need to learn how to cook more diverse meals, living on pasta and noodles isn't sustainable or healthy. Maybe try some simple recipes this weekend.

Post-midterm lull. Caught up on sleep. Went into town and bought a warmer scarf and gloves - winter is definitely coming. Started preliminary work on the Text Analytics project with Aoife's group. Brainstorming datasets and approach for sentiment analysis.

Feeling the pre-Diwali homesickness. Family celebrations starting back home. Trying to focus on the ML project - implementing and comparing SVM and Random Forest. Hyperparameter tuning for SVM is taking ages using GridSearchCV.

Finished packing. Room looks bare. Reflecting on the semester - challenging but learned so much. Distributed Systems was the hardest, Cloud Computing the most immediately practical. Looking forward to seeing family and recharging before Semester 2.

Setting up development environments for Semester 2 modules. Installing PyTorch, Hugging Face Transformers, SQL clients, speech analysis tools like Praat. Ensuring everything works is step zero for all the assignments. Feels like starting fresh.

Weekend dedicated to LeetCode for the upcoming coding assessment. Focused on Medium problems, trying to improve speed and identify patterns (e.g., two pointers, sliding window, BFS/DFS). It's a skill that needs constant practice.

content: Prepping for two interviews next week: SWE technical screen and Cloud Support behavioural/scenario round. Different skills needed. Practicing coding aloud for the first, thinking through troubleshooting steps for the second. Busy weekend ahead.

Post-final round interviews. Feeling drained but hopeful. Spent today catching up on UCD emails and working on the Gen AI project - preprocessing the scraped module description data. Tedious but necessary step before fine-tuning. Trying to distract myself from obsessively checking emails for the interview result.

Received the official MSc transcript via email. Seeing all the modules and grades listed formally is satisfying. Especially that A+ in Gen AI! Saved multiple copies. This will be needed for the visa application and for the employer.

Attended another apartment viewing. Still no luck. The competition is fierce. Starting to feel anxious about finding a place before the job starts. Considering expanding my search area, even if it means a longer commute.
Exploring the Rathmines library. Smaller than UCD's but cozy. Signed up for a library card. Nice to have a quiet place to read or work outside the house. Starting to feel part of the local community.

Did a big grocery shop and meal prep for the week ahead. Trying to get into good habits before the structure of work begins. Also laid out clothes for the first day. Small things to reduce first-day anxiety.
